hero.headline: Senate Committee to Vote on Digital Replica Rights Bill
hero.body:
The Senate Judiciary Committee is scheduled to vote today on the NO FAKES Act of 2026, legislation that would establish new intellectual property protections for individuals seeking to control digital replicas of their voice and likeness. The bill's full name, Nurture Originals, Foster Art, and Keep Entertainment Safe, signals its focus on protecting creative professionals in an era of advancing artificial intelligence.

Under the proposed legislation, individuals would gain the legal right to authorize or block the creation and use of digital replicas that mimic their voice or physical appearance. The measure addresses growing concerns in the entertainment industry about unauthorized use of performer likenesses in AI-generated content. Industry figures have advocated for the legislation as technology has made it increasingly simple to create convincing digital reproductions of real people without their consent.

The committee vote represents a key procedural step for the bill. If advanced by the Judiciary Committee, the legislation would move closer to consideration by the full Senate. The proposal has drawn support from music and entertainment industry leaders who argue that existing intellectual property law does not adequately address the challenges posed by AI technology.

The legislation would create a new category of intellectual property rights distinct from existing copyright, trademark, and right of publicity laws. Supporters argue the measure is necessary to protect performers, actors, musicians, and other public figures from having their digital likenesses exploited without permission or compensation. The bill would apply to both living individuals and the estates of deceased persons, allowing families to control posthumous uses of a person's voice or image.

The timing of the committee vote reflects broader legislative efforts to establish regulatory frameworks for artificial intelligence applications across multiple sectors. The entertainment industry has emerged as an early flashpoint in debates over AI regulation, with questions about digital replicas intersecting with ongoing discussions about copyright, labor rights, and creative compensation in an increasingly automated production environment.

cards.headline: US and Iran sign agreement to end hostilities and reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding that took effect immediately after both countries finalized the agreement. President Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian signed the document on Wednesday, according to Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who served as the lead mediator in the negotiations.

The agreement marks a significant development in US-Iran relations, bringing an end to armed conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global energy supplies. Roughly one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied fossil gas passes through the narrow shipping channel during peacetime. The deal follows months of military engagement and tension between the two countries, with Pakistan playing a central role in facilitating the talks.

The 14-paragraph memo includes provisions ending the fighting and addresses Iran's nuclear program. The agreement also includes a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. President Trump has emphasized that the deal ensures Iran will never buy, develop, or produce a nuclear weapon.

Trump publicly defended the agreement, framing it as necessary to stabilize the region and restore normal shipping routes through the strait. The closure of the waterway had created serious economic consequences worldwide, with fuel price increases and supply disruptions affecting countries dependent on Gulf oil imports. Germany halved its 2026 growth forecast, while Greece announced additional economic aid for households and farmers struggling with increased energy costs.

The humanitarian impact of the conflict has been substantial. According to the International Maritime Organization, approximately 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships have been stranded in the Gulf since the strait's closure. The UN maritime agency has appealed for assistance for the stranded workers.

Despite the agreement, significant challenges remain unresolved. The text of the agreement regarding Iran's nuclear program falls short of Trump's public claims about the deal's guarantees. Critics argue that the most difficult aspects of US-Iran relations remain unaddressed, and the longer-term issues will require future negotiations to resolve. Some observers characterize the agreement as a return to conditions existing before the conflict began, rather than a comprehensive resolution of the underlying disputes.

Both sides have committed to the agreement's terms by signing the document, signaling their intention to move forward with implementation. The immediate effect means that provisions regarding the cessation of hostilities and the reopening of the strait are now in force. Pakistan's Prime Minister Sharif stated that the signing demonstrated genuine commitment from both Washington and Tehran to follow through on the outlined steps, though he acknowledged that talks scheduled in Islamabad did not proceed as originally planned.

cards.headline: Tropical Storm Arthur brings flooding and tornadoes to Gulf Coast
cards.teaser: Tropical Storm Arthur pushed ashore in the Deep South on Wednesday, bringing widespread flooding and tornado-warned storms to the Gulf Coast.
cards.body:
Tropical Storm Arthur pushed ashore in the Deep South on Wednesday, bringing widespread flooding and tornado-warned storms to the Gulf Coast. The storm created a rare high flood risk across the region, forcing local officials to mobilize emergency preparations.

New Orleans leaders outlined storm preparations as the system approached, with significant flood threats expected to continue into Thursday morning. The Washington Post reported dangerous downpours moving inland, while weather monitoring systems tracked tornado warnings across multiple Gulf Coast communities.

The storm caused damage across the region, with WDSU documenting widespread flooding in affected areas. CNN meteorologists noted that Arthur's circulation pattern was fueling both the tornado threat and the unusually high flood risk, a combination that presented dual hazards for coastal and inland communities alike.

The National Weather Service issued a First Alert for the significant flood threat, warning residents that dangerous conditions would persist through early Thursday. Arthur's slow movement allowed rainfall to accumulate in affected areas, increasing the risk of flash flooding and river flooding across the Deep South.

Emergency management officials coordinated response efforts across multiple states as the storm system continued to produce heavy rainfall and severe weather. The combination of flooding rain and tornado potential required residents to monitor both flood warnings and severe thunderstorm alerts simultaneously, complicating evacuation and shelter decisions for those in the storm's path.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth announces review of US troops in Europe
cards.teaser: Secretary of Defense Hegseth announced a six-month review of American forces stationed in Europe while criticizing some NATO allies.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a comprehensive review of U.S. military forces in Europe during remarks in Brussels, calling for a "NATO 3.0" overhaul of the alliance. He criticized NATO allies for what he called an "era of free-riding," warning that some countries will fail the assessment while others pass with flying colors.

Hegseth made clear that U.S. contributions to NATO will be contingent on allies meeting defense spending targets. He emphasized that the review aims to shift Europe toward taking primary responsibility for its own defense and that NATO must become a "two-way street" where the U.S. adjusts its commitment based on allied spending levels.

cards.headline: Average U.S. Gas Price Falls Below $4 After Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Drivers are seeing relief at the pump following the U.S.-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
The average price of gasoline in the United States dropped below $4 per gallon for the first time in months following a preliminary agreement between the U.S. and Iran. The deal includes an end to fighting and an agreement that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, along with a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. The accord also reopens the Strait of Hormuz, restoring oil flows from the Persian Gulf.

Despite the gas price decline and positive stock market movement after the agreement, British economic officials have cautioned that inflation pressures will persist. The Bank of England kept interest rates unchanged, citing ongoing uncertainty from the conflict's economic impact.

cards.headline: Ukraine Launches Largest Drone Strike on Moscow Since War Began
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces struck Moscow with nearly 200 drones in what officials confirmed as the largest aerial assault on the Russian capital since the start of the full-scale invasion. The operation targeted a major oil refinery and other locations in the southeastern areas of the city, forcing the temporary closure of Russia's biggest airport and setting multiple sites ablaze.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy characterized the attack as retaliation for Russia's earlier strike on a historic monastery complex in Kyiv. The operation demonstrated Ukraine's continued capacity to conduct large-scale coordinated strikes against Russian infrastructure deep within the country, despite the presence of air defense networks around the capital.

The assault struck a refinery and a shopping center, both catching fire from the drone impacts. Moscow's airports halted operations for several hours as authorities managed the security threat and worked to clear the airspace. Flight operations eventually resumed after the immediate danger passed.

Russian air defense systems engaged the incoming drones throughout the operation, though officials have not disclosed how many were successfully intercepted compared to those reaching their targets. Similarly, Russian authorities have provided limited information about the full extent of damage to the refinery or other struck facilities, or any casualties resulting from the attack.

The strike reflected an ongoing pattern of Ukrainian targeting of Russian energy infrastructure and military assets located far from active front lines. These operations have intensified in recent months as Ukraine seeks to disrupt Russia's economy and military capabilities. The scale and coordination of this particular assault underscored Ukraine's ability to maintain offensive operations despite Russian defensive measures.

The attack occurred amid broader developments in the conflict. Peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia have accelerated in recent weeks, with Ukrainian officials suggesting a deal was substantially advanced. Zelenskyy stated that a potential agreement was nearing completion, though significant disagreements remained on critical issues including territorial control and security guarantees.

This drone operation also came after Moscow made claims that Ukraine had attempted to strike one of Putin's official residences in northwestern Russia days earlier. Ukrainian officials denied these accusations, characterizing them as false claims intended to undermine ongoing peace discussions. The CIA reportedly determined that no such attack had taken place, contradicting Russian assertions.

The strike also highlighted the broader military picture in the region. Ukrainian officials noted increased Russian drone activity along Belarus's border, with intelligence drones from Russian-controlled airspace entering Ukraine from Belarusian territory. In response, Ukraine has strengthened defensive fortifications along its northern border, adding obstacles and reinforcing positions against potential new threats.

The Moscow drone strike represented a significant demonstration of Ukrainian military capability and resolve, occurring against the backdrop of diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the nearly four-year conflict.

cards.headline: Trump demands complicate Republican legislative priorities in Congress
cards.teaser: GOP lawmakers face tension as the president's recent requests arrive as they near completion of key policy objectives.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's interim deal with Iran has created fresh tensions within the Republican party. Several Senate Republicans, including Senator Bill Cassidy, have publicly criticized the agreement, calling it "the worst foreign policy blunder in decades." The accord, released Wednesday, includes significant political and financial concessions to Iran in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and averting economic crisis.

The deal's controversial terms have exposed divisions among GOP lawmakers, complicating efforts to maintain party unity. Republicans are now grappling with the administration's foreign policy direction while attempting to advance their broader legislative agenda in Congress.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Reaches Initial Agreement with Iran
cards.teaser: The deal grants Iran economic relief in exchange for minimal concessions, delaying more difficult negotiations.
cards.body:
The Trump administration signed a preliminary agreement with Iran to end fighting and open the Strait of Hormuz. The 14-paragraph memo includes a commitment that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons and establishes a $300 billion redevelopment package for the country. The deal postpones more difficult negotiations for future talks.

Israeli officials expressed strong opposition to the agreement, with analysts concluding it fails to achieve Israel's stated war objectives. According to regional experts, the deal leaves Israel in a worse position regarding each of its primary aims in the region.

cards.headline: Gunfire and Explosions Reported at Niger Airport
cards.teaser: Witnesses reported sounds of gunfire and explosions at the airport in Niger's capital.
cards.body:
Gunfire and explosions were reported at the airport in Niger's capital. The country has been battling a militant Islamist insurgency for the past decade, with security forces conducting ongoing operations against extremist groups in the region.

The same airport was targeted by suspected jihadists in January, underscoring its vulnerability to militant attacks. Niger continues to face significant security threats from insurgent groups operating across the country.

cards.headline: Russian Shadow Fleet Vessel Enters English Channel
cards.teaser: A Russian-flagged ship entered the Channel days after another vessel was boarded by authorities.
cards.body:
The Forwarder, a Russian-flagged ship, has entered the English Channel following its departure from Primorsk port last week. The vessel transited the waterway on Wednesday evening, marking the first Russian shadow fleet ship to pass through since authorities boarded the Smyrtos.

Shadow fleet vessels are used to circumvent international sanctions by transporting goods outside conventional shipping channels. The Forwarder's passage occurs as Western nations intensify monitoring of Russian maritime activities.

cards.headline: Lawyer in Uganda Treason Case Charged
cards.teaser: Ugandan authorities charged a defense lawyer in a high-profile treason case with a related offense.
cards.body:
Erias Lukwago, a lawyer representing defendants in a high-profile Ugandan treason case, was arrested this week and charged with a related offence. The attorney had been providing legal representation to individuals accused of treason by the government.

Uganda's military chief had previously made public threats against Lukwago, boasting of the "hurt and pain" he would inflict on the lawyer. The arrest and charges raise serious concerns about the independence of the legal profession and the treatment of defense attorneys in politically sensitive cases.

cards.headline: Suspected Gang Leader Killed in Airport Ambush
cards.teaser: Gunmen concealed weapons in flower bouquets and stuffed toys before shooting their target at an Ecuadorian airport.
cards.body:
A suspected gang leader was shot dead outside Guayaquil airport in Ecuador in an ambush carried out by gunmen who concealed their weapons behind flower bouquets and stuffed toys. The attackers used the decorative items to hide their firearms while waiting for the victim.

The killing reflects the escalating violence in Ecuador, where organized crime groups are locked in competition over control of drug trafficking routes.

cards.headline: Ancient Oak Tree Associated with Robin Hood Legend Dies
cards.teaser: A centuries-old oak tree in Sherwood Forest said to have sheltered Robin Hood has died.
cards.body:
Sherwood Forest's Major Oak, thought to have stood for over 1,000 years in Nottinghamshire, has died. The tree was one of the world's most famous and a significant landmark in the historic forest, long believed to have sheltered the legendary outlaw Robin Hood.

The loss represents a major cultural and historical blow to the region. The ancient oak held deep significance for those connected to the area and the enduring Robin Hood legend.

hero.headline: Obama Presidential Center dedication ceremony takes place Thursday
hero.teaser: The grand opening of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago will feature a star-studded dedication ceremony.
hero.body:
The Obama Presidential Center will be dedicated Thursday on the South Side of Chicago, marking the official opening of a facility that distinguishes itself from traditional presidential libraries through its emphasis on art and community spaces.

The privately funded $850 million center sits on a 19-acre campus in Jackson Park, close to where Barack Obama lived as a young man and began his political career. The facility includes a museum housed in a distinctive 225-foot granite structure, along with a branch of the Chicago Public Library, an NBA-regulation basketball court, a recording studio and a sledding hill.

What sets the Obama Presidential Center apart is its unprecedented commissioning of original artworks. Barack and Michelle Obama selected 30 artists from diverse backgrounds to create works throughout the campus. Valerie Jarrett, chief executive of the Obama Foundation, explained the vision behind the art collection. "We want people who come here to look at a piece of art, stand next to a stranger, have a conversation about that piece of art and how it touches them each in their own individual ways," she said.

The artworks are integrated throughout the campus. Martin Puryear created a monumental sculpture titled Bending the Arc, inspired by Martin Luther King Jr.'s statement about the moral arc of the universe. Richard Hunt's Book Bird, located in the library reading garden, depicts a bird emerging from book pages to represent the transformative power of reading. This was Hunt's final work before his death in 2023.

Other notable pieces include a painted glass window by Ethiopian American artist Julie Mehretu titled Uprising of the Sun, and Mark Bradford's City of the Big Shoulders, a 38-foot-tall textured painting mapping Chicago and Lake Michigan. A mixed-media portrait of Barack and Michelle Obama by Njideka Akunyili Crosby marks the first artwork created of the two together.

The center also features the Ann Dunham Water Terrace, named for Obama's mother, which includes a stone water feature by Maya Lin. Inside the museum, Idris Khan's Sky of Hope fills the ceiling of the Nelson Mandela Sky Room with thousands of hand-stamped words from Obama's speeches honoring civil rights leaders.

Louise Bernard, the museum's founding director, noted that artists were given creative freedom. "The artists were really thinking about the Obama legacy: a sense of hopefulness, a sense of connection to place, the power of place," she said.

The Obama Presidential Center also represents a departure from other presidential libraries by divorcing itself from the National Archives and Records Administration. Rather than housing millions of physical federal documents, the center is funding their digitization while storing physical records elsewhere.

The grand opening ceremony is expected to draw prominent attendees for the official public opening after years of planning and construction.

cards.headline: Nearly 200 Ukrainian drones strike Moscow area in largest attack of war
cards.teaser: Ukraine launched its largest drone attack on Moscow since the start of the full-scale war, hitting a refinery and shopping center.
cards.body:
Almost 200 Ukrainian drones struck the Moscow region southeast of the capital on Wednesday in Ukraine's largest air raid on the city since the full-scale war began. The attack set a major oil refinery ablaze and also hit a shopping centre. The strikes forced evacuations at Russia's largest airport.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as retaliation for Russia's strike on a historic monastery complex in Kyiv earlier in the week.

cards.headline: Church of England apologizes for role in forced adoptions
cards.teaser: The Church of England issued an apology for pressuring thousands of unmarried women to give up their babies between 1949 and 1976.
cards.body:
The Church of England apologized for its role in forced adoptions that affected thousands of unmarried women over nearly three decades. The practice involved pressuring women to relinquish their babies during a period spanning from 1949 to 1976.

The church acknowledged its participation in a system that separated mothers from their children based on marital status. The apology comes decades after the practice ended, addressing a period when social stigma against unmarried mothers led to widespread coerced adoptions.

cards.headline: First Russian shadow fleet vessel enters English Channel since Smyrtos boarding
cards.teaser: A Russian-flagged ship entered the English Channel on Wednesday, the first such vessel since the Smyrtos boarding incident.
cards.body:
Forwarder, a Russian-flagged vessel, entered the English Channel on Wednesday evening after departing from Primorsk port the previous week. This marks the first transit by a Russian shadow fleet ship through the Channel since the Smyrtos boarding incident.

Shadow fleet vessels transport Russian goods, particularly oil, while evading international sanctions. The Forwarder's passage signals a resumption of such transits through this strategically important waterway.

cards.headline: England beats Croatia 4-2 despite defensive concerns
cards.teaser: England scored four goals in a win over Croatia but showed vulnerability on defense throughout the match.
cards.body:
England made a winning start to their World Cup 2026 campaign with a 4-2 victory over Croatia in Dallas. Harry Kane equalled Gary Lineker's record for England World Cup goals with a penalty and a header from Declan Rice's corner, but Croatia equalized twice before half-time.

Thomas Tuchel's half-time speech proved pivotal, with Kane revealing the coach told the team to "show the world what we can be." England's second-half performance improved dramatically, with Jude Bellingham re-establishing their lead before Marcus Rashford sealed the victory late on.

hero.headline: Bank of England Holds Interest Rates at 3.75% Amid Iran Deal Uncertainty
hero.body:
The Bank of England maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.75%, deciding to hold steady as policymakers assess the impact of the recently signed U.S.-Iran peace deal on inflation and economic growth.

The decision reflects caution about how quickly the agreement will translate into relief for British consumers and businesses. While the deal aims to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and normalize oil supplies, Bank of England officials warned that inflationary pressures will likely persist in the near term.

The central bank last reduced rates in December before Middle East tensions escalated and halted further cuts. The conflict had disrupted global oil shipments and pushed energy prices higher across Europe and beyond. Although the peace agreement offers promise, policymakers emphasized that the full economic impact remains uncertain and could take time to materialize.

Bank officials acknowledged that inflation will not disappear simply because the Iran conflict has ended. The price pressures that existed before the war remain unresolved. Energy costs spiked during the fighting and fed into broader price increases throughout the British economy. Central bankers must now determine whether the peace agreement will provide sustained relief or if other factors will keep inflation elevated.

The decision to hold rates reflects the Bank's balancing act between supporting economic growth and controlling inflation. Policymakers want concrete evidence that inflation is cooling before easing monetary policy. They are not willing to assume that geopolitical developments will automatically lower prices for consumers and businesses.

The cautious stance contrasts with some market expectations that had anticipated potential rate cuts following the Iran deal announcement. The decision signals that central bankers prefer to wait for hard data showing cooling inflation rather than acting on optimism about the agreement's economic effects.

Job vacancy data released alongside the decision showed openings at a five-year low, suggesting businesses are growing more cautious about hiring. Companies appear to be waiting to see how the geopolitical situation stabilizes before committing to expansion plans. The figures indicate that economic uncertainty continues to weigh on business confidence despite the peace agreement.

The Bank of England's approach mirrors caution being shown by central banks globally. Other monetary authorities are similarly holding rates steady as they monitor how the Iran deal affects inflation and growth worldwide. The decision underscores the challenge facing policymakers in balancing competing economic pressures at a time of significant geopolitical change.

For British households and businesses, the decision means interest rates will remain at current levels for now. Further cuts remain unlikely until the Bank sees clearer signs that inflation is moving back toward its target level.

cards.headline: Average U.S. Gas Price Falls Below $4 After Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Drivers are seeing relief at the pump following the U.S.-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
The average price of gasoline in the United States dropped below $4 per gallon for the first time in months following a preliminary agreement between the U.S. and Iran. The deal includes an end to fighting and an agreement that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, along with a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. The accord also reopens the Strait of Hormuz, restoring oil flows from the Persian Gulf.

Despite the gas price decline and positive stock market movement after the agreement, British economic officials have cautioned that inflation pressures will persist. The Bank of England kept interest rates unchanged, citing ongoing uncertainty from the conflict's economic impact.

cards.headline: Apple to Raise iPhone Prices, CEO Tim Cook Says
cards.teaser: Apple CEO Tim Cook said price increases are unavoidable due to rising memory chip costs.
cards.body:
Apple plans to raise prices on its products due to soaring memory chip costs driven by the AI boom. CEO Tim Cook told The Wall Street Journal that price increases are "unavoidable," explaining that the company faces huge cost increases it can no longer fully absorb for customers.

The memory shortage has affected tech manufacturers industry-wide as demand for advanced semiconductors intensifies. Cook did not specify which products would see price increases or when the changes would take effect.

cards.headline: Stock Futures Rise Following Iran Deal and Rate Decision
cards.teaser: U.S. stock futures climbed as investors digested the U.S.-Iran agreement and Federal Reserve rate outlook.
cards.body:
Stock index futures rose as markets reacted to the U.S.-Iran deal and assessed expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate policy. The Nasdaq was set to rebound after recent declines, with futures indicating gains across major indexes. Optimism about the Iran agreement, which is expected to ease energy price pressures, helped lift investor sentiment.

The gains came as markets balanced relief over the geopolitical development against concerns about potential Federal Reserve rate hikes. Gasoline prices falling below $4 per gallon added to the positive mood, suggesting inflation pressures may begin to ease. Technology shares showed particular strength in premarket trading as investors anticipated improved economic conditions.

cards.headline: SpaceX Shares Soar in Trading Debut
cards.teaser: Retail investors drove SpaceX shares higher in the company's blockbuster public market debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX made its public market debut on the Nasdaq with a company valuation of $2.2 trillion, marking the largest IPO ever. The strong trading performance was driven by significant demand from individual investors, demonstrating their growing influence in financial markets.

The milestone also propelled founder Elon Musk to become the world's first trillionaire, with a net worth of $1.11 trillion according to the Bloomberg rich list. Musk previously stated he had given SpaceX less than a 10% chance of success when the company first started.

cards.headline: UK Job Vacancies Hit Five-Year Low
cards.teaser: British companies are growing more cautious about hiring as job openings reach their lowest level in five years.
cards.body:
The number of job vacancies in the United Kingdom has fallen to a five-year low, with new figures showing that companies are becoming more cautious about hiring. The decline reflects growing uncertainty among businesses about economic conditions and future demand.

The data indicates a cooling labor market as employers pull back on expansion plans. This pullback coincides with the Bank of England's decision to hold interest rates steady, suggesting both policymakers and businesses are taking a cautious stance amid economic and geopolitical uncertainty.

cards.headline: Flight Prices May Stay High Despite Iran Deal
cards.teaser: Airline ticket prices may remain elevated for months even as the Iran agreement eases fuel costs.
cards.body:
The Iran conflict that began on February 28 disrupted energy production and transportation across the Middle East, causing fuel costs to jump. The U.S.-Iran agreement includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway expected to help reduce jet fuel prices.

However, passengers may not see immediate relief at the pump or ticket counter. Airlines have learned that travelers will pay higher fares, which could limit how much carriers reduce prices even as fuel costs decline. The lag time between fuel price adjustments and airline pricing strategies means ticket prices may remain elevated for months.

hero.headline: Waymo recalls nearly 4,000 robotaxis after vehicles entered construction zones
hero.body:
Waymo has issued a recall affecting nearly 4,000 of its autonomous vehicles after identifying instances where the robotaxis drove into highway sections that were closed for construction. The company has documented at least 13 separate occasions where its self-driving cars entered restricted construction areas.

The recall represents a significant safety concern for the autonomous vehicle industry, as construction zones present unique challenges with temporary signage, altered traffic patterns, and active work crews. Waymo operates one of the largest commercial robotaxi fleets in the United States, providing ride-hailing services in several cities including San Francisco and Phoenix.

The incidents raise questions about how autonomous driving systems interpret temporary road closures and construction signage. Unlike permanent road features that can be mapped in advance, construction zones often appear suddenly and rely on temporary barriers, cones, and signs that self-driving systems must recognize and respond to in real time. The recall will address software issues that prevented the vehicles from properly identifying and avoiding these closed-off areas.

Waymo has been expanding its robotaxi operations across multiple markets, positioning itself as a leader in the commercialization of self-driving technology. The company, owned by Alphabet, has logged millions of autonomous miles and regularly touts its safety record compared to human drivers. This recall, however, highlights the ongoing technical challenges facing the industry as it works to navigate complex and changing road conditions.

The company has not disclosed whether any accidents, injuries, or property damage resulted from the vehicles entering construction zones. The recall will involve updating the software systems that control how the vehicles detect and respond to temporary road closures. Waymo continues to operate its fleet while implementing the fixes across its nearly 4,000-vehicle fleet.

cards.headline: NASA selects Eric Schmidt-backed rocket company for Mars mission
cards.teaser: Relativity Space will compete with SpaceX to reach Mars after winning a NASA contract.
cards.body:
NASA has selected Relativity Space, a rocket manufacturer acquired by former Google executive chair Eric Schmidt, for a Mars mission. The company previously faced challenges in reaching orbit before Schmidt's acquisition last year.

The contract positions Relativity Space as a competitor to SpaceX in the race to Mars. Despite SpaceX's head start in deep space missions, Relativity Space now has an opportunity to establish itself as a credible player in the space launch industry.

cards.headline: Scientists discover garnet in Mars meteorite
cards.teaser: Researchers found the mineral garnet inside a Martian meteorite that landed on Earth.
cards.body:
Scientists examining a meteorite from Mars discovered garnet, a mineral not previously found in Martian samples. The University of Trieste announced the finding, which adds new information to the geological history of the red planet.

The mineral discovery may help reveal how Mars evolved billions of years ago. Researchers believe the presence of garnet could provide clues about the conditions and processes that shaped the planet's crust and interior during its early development.

cards.headline: Epic announces Unreal Engine 6 and pays developers $1 billion
cards.teaser: Epic Games revealed Unreal Engine 6 will unify UE5 and UEFN into a single engine.
cards.body:
Epic Games announced Unreal Engine 6 at State of Unreal 2026, merging its current UE5 platform with UEFN into a single unified engine. The company also revealed it has distributed $1 billion to developers working on the UEFN platform. Unreal Engine 5.8 was announced as an intermediate release focused on optimization improvements leading up to the sixth generation.

Epic plans to enable Fortnite players to use their character skins across other games, reflecting the company's broader strategy to create an interconnected gaming ecosystem that extends beyond its flagship battle royale title.

cards.headline: Pixi launches iOS app for augmented reality messaging
cards.teaser: The new app transforms text messages into interactive AR experiences on iOS devices.
cards.body:
Pixi has released an iOS app that transforms text messages into interactive augmented reality experiences. The company is positioning AR as the next evolution in mobile messaging, moving beyond traditional stickers, GIFs, and emoji reactions.

The app enables users to create and share three-dimensional interactive content directly within their messaging conversations, representing Pixi's vision that AR will become a standard communication feature on smartphones.

cards.headline: Apple CEO says AI costs may force iPhone price increases
cards.teaser: Tim Cook described the current pricing situation as unsustainable in a recent interview.
cards.body:
Apple CEO Tim Cook has stated that rising AI costs are creating pricing pressures for the company. Cook indicated the current financial situation is unsustainable as Apple invests in developing and integrating artificial intelligence features across its product line.

While Cook acknowledged that prices may need to increase, he did not specify when such increases would occur or which products would be affected. The comments reflect Apple's challenge in managing the substantial expenses associated with AI development while remaining competitive as other companies rapidly advance their own AI capabilities.

cards.headline: New video game receives reviews comparing it to Zelda and Final Fantasy
cards.teaser: The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales launched on Switch 2 to mixed critical reception.
cards.body:
The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales has been reviewed by major gaming outlets following its release on the Switch 2. The Guardian described it as a playable tribute to the Zelda series, while The Verge highlighted its combination of Final Fantasy and Zelda elements.

Game Informer titled its review 'History Repeats Itself,' and Nintendo Life compiled multiple perspectives on the game. The title represents an attempt to blend mechanics and aesthetics from two of gaming's most influential franchises into a new intellectual property.

hero.headline: Trae Young to decline player option, become free agent
hero.teaser: Wizards star Trae Young plans to decline his $48.97 million player option and enter free agency, though Washington remains the front-runner to re-sign him.
hero.body:
Wizards star Trae Young plans to decline his $48.97 million player option for the 2026-27 season and become a free agent, according to sources. The decision will allow Young to negotiate a new contract, potentially on a longer-term deal.

Despite opting out, Washington remains the front-runner to retain Young's services. The point guard has been a central figure for the Wizards, and the team is expected to make a strong push to keep him in the nation's capital. Young's decision to decline the option is a common strategy for star players seeking long-term security and maximum earnings.

cards.headline: Knicks owner Dolan says team will not enter second luxury tax apron
cards.teaser: New York Knicks owner James Dolan told WFAN radio Wednesday that he will not allow the team to enter the punitive second luxury tax apron for the 2026-27 season.
cards.body:
New York Knicks owner James Dolan announced Wednesday on WFAN radio that he will not allow the team to enter the second luxury tax apron for the 2026-27 season. The statement comes after the Knicks won their first NBA championship in 53 years.

The decision sets a financial boundary for the organization as it plans its roster for next season. Dolan's position means the front office will need to make difficult choices about which players to retain while remaining below the second apron threshold.

cards.headline: North Carolina advances to Men's College World Series finals
cards.teaser: North Carolina defeated West Virginia 12-7 to reach the Men's College World Series finals for the first time since 2007, where they will face Oklahoma.
cards.body:
Owen Hull had a triple and two doubles among his four hits as North Carolina rolled past West Virginia 12-7 on Wednesday to advance to the Men's College World Series finals. The Tar Heels will face Oklahoma in the championship series.

The victory marks North Carolina's first appearance in the MCWS finals since 2007. Hull's offensive performance paced the Tar Heels' attack, helping the team pull away from West Virginia. North Carolina will now seek its first national championship in the sport against Oklahoma, which won its semifinal matchup to reach the finals.

cards.headline: Aces advance to Commissioner's Cup final with win over Mercury
cards.teaser: The Las Vegas Aces defeated the Phoenix Mercury 86-76 behind A'ja Wilson's performance to reach the WNBA Commissioner's Cup championship game for the third time.
cards.body:
The Las Vegas Aces defeated the Phoenix Mercury 86-76 on Wednesday night to advance to the WNBA Commissioner's Cup championship game. This marks the third time the Aces have reached the final in the in-season tournament's history.

A'ja Wilson led the Aces' offensive effort in the semifinal victory. Las Vegas will await the outcome of the other semifinal matchup to learn their opponent for the championship game.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark unveils first signature Nike shoe
cards.teaser: Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark announced her first signature basketball shoe, the Caitlin 1, on Wednesday afternoon.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark announced her first signature shoe, the Caitlin 1, on Wednesday afternoon. The Nike basketball shoe represents a major endorsement milestone for the Indiana Fever guard.

Clark joins a select group of WNBA players with signature shoe deals. The announcement comes during her rookie season in the WNBA after a record-breaking college career at Iowa. Nike has invested heavily in women's basketball in recent years, and Clark's signature line reflects her marketability and impact on the sport.

cards.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo says Portugal's World Cup hopes alive after opening draw
cards.teaser: Cristiano Ronaldo defended Portugal's performance against Congo DR in their World Cup opener and said the team is already focused on the next match.
cards.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo defended Portugal's opening match performance against Congo DR at the World Cup, insisting the tournament is far from over for his team. The Portuguese captain emphasized he is already focused on the next group stage game rather than dwelling on the result.

Ronaldo's comments reflect confidence in Portugal's ability to bounce back from their opening draw and advance through the group stage.

cards.headline: Cincinnati denies knowing of Sorsby's gambling violations in 2024
cards.teaser: Cincinnati responded to claims from Brendan Sorsby's agent, saying the school would never knowingly play an athlete who violated NCAA gambling rules.
cards.body:
Cincinnati issued a statement Wednesday denying it knowingly played quarterback Brendan Sorsby while he was violating NCAA gambling rules. The response came after Sorsby's agent publicly questioned how the school handled the quarterback's gambling activities in 2024.

The school reaffirmed its policy against playing athletes who breach NCAA regulations, which prohibit sports betting. Sorsby's agent had raised concerns about the school's awareness of the gambling violations and when that knowledge was obtained.

hero.headline: Senate Committee to Vote on Digital Replica Rights Bill
hero.body:
The Senate Judiciary Committee is scheduled to vote today on the NO FAKES Act of 2026, legislation that would establish new intellectual property protections for individuals seeking to control digital replicas of their voice and likeness. The bill's full name, Nurture Originals, Foster Art, and Keep Entertainment Safe, signals its focus on protecting creative professionals in an era of advancing artificial intelligence.

Under the proposed legislation, individuals would gain the legal right to authorize or block the creation and use of digital replicas that mimic their voice or physical appearance. The measure addresses growing concerns in the entertainment industry about unauthorized use of performer likenesses in AI-generated content. Industry figures have advocated for the legislation as technology has made it increasingly simple to create convincing digital reproductions of real people without their consent.

The committee vote represents a key procedural step for the bill. If advanced by the Judiciary Committee, the legislation would move closer to consideration by the full Senate. The proposal has drawn support from music and entertainment industry leaders who argue that existing intellectual property law does not adequately address the challenges posed by AI technology.

The legislation would create a new category of intellectual property rights distinct from existing copyright, trademark, and right of publicity laws. Supporters argue the measure is necessary to protect performers, actors, musicians, and other public figures from having their digital likenesses exploited without permission or compensation. The bill would apply to both living individuals and the estates of deceased persons, allowing families to control posthumous uses of a person's voice or image.

The timing of the committee vote reflects broader legislative efforts to establish regulatory frameworks for artificial intelligence applications across multiple sectors. The entertainment industry has emerged as an early flashpoint in debates over AI regulation, with questions about digital replicas intersecting with ongoing discussions about copyright, labor rights, and creative compensation in an increasingly automated production environment.

cards.headline: Netflix Animated Film Spends Full Year on Top 10 List
cards.teaser: KPop Demon Hunters has remained on Netflix's Top 10 list for 52 consecutive weeks since its release.
cards.body:
"KPop Demon Hunters" reaches its one-year anniversary on June 20, having occupied Netflix's Top 10 list for all 52 weeks since its release. The animated feature has achieved the rare milestone of remaining in the platform's top rankings throughout an entire year.

The film's sustained performance demonstrates both critical and commercial success, establishing it as a notable achievement in the streaming landscape.

cards.headline: Steven Sater and James Bourne Release Musical Concept Album
cards.teaser: The creators of Murder at the Gates are releasing a concept album featuring Gaten Matarazzo and other performers.
cards.body:
Steven Sater and James Bourne are releasing a concept album for their musical Murder at the Gates on July 1, 2026. The album features vocals from Stranger Things actor Gaten Matarazzo, Milo Manheim, Joy Woods, and other performers. A preview track titled "Fuckin Scream" featuring Matarazzo was released ahead of the full album.

Sater is an award-winning theatrical composer and lyricist who has won Tony, Grammy, and Olivier Awards. The concept album allows listeners to experience the musical's songs in advance of any potential stage production.

cards.headline: Jakarta Announces Tax Incentives to Attract Film Production
cards.teaser: Indonesia's capital city unveiled a six-point initiative to become a regional production hub and expanded its Netflix partnership.
cards.body:
Jakarta Vice Governor Rano Karno presented a package of tax rebates and production incentives at the APOS conference in Bali aimed at making the city a leading film production destination in Southeast Asia. The centerpiece of the initiative is a tax incentive program designed to attract domestic and international productions to the capital.

Karno also held discussions with Netflix executives about expanding the streaming service's production output in Jakarta. The announcements reflect Jakarta's effort to compete with other regional production centers for entertainment industry investment and job creation.

cards.headline: London Museum Smithfield Location to Open in November
cards.teaser: The museum's new Smithfield site will house works including a Banksy piece and historic documents.
cards.body:
The London Museum announced its Smithfield building will open to the public in November. The new location will display Banksy's piranhas artwork and the United Kingdom's oldest hand-written document among its collection.

The opening marks the establishment of a permanent home for the museum's holdings at the Smithfield site. The venue will provide expanded space for the institution's historical and contemporary art collections.

cards.headline: UK Rapper Thanks Linkin Park After Band Member Notices Freestyle
cards.teaser: Mike Shinoda from Linkin Park spotted a freestyle performance by Megan Da Savage on an independent music platform.
cards.body:
UK rapper Megan Da Savage thanked Linkin Park after band member Mike Shinoda acknowledged her freestyle performance. Shinoda said he discovered the rapper's work on an independent music platform.

The interaction between the established rock band member and emerging artist highlights how digital platforms allow musicians to share work and connect across different genres and career stages.

cards.headline: Turkish Director Presents New Film at Transilvania Festival
cards.teaser: Belkis Bayrak is developing A Brighter Word Than Bright, a feature exploring grief and resilience.
cards.body:
Turkish filmmaker Belkis Bayrak presented her second feature film A Brighter Word Than Bright at the Transilvania International Film Festival's co-production forum this week. The film examines grief and resilience in the aftermath of suicide.

Bayrak's debut feature Glizar premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and played in the San Sebastian Film Festival's New Directors Competition. The director is building on her festival presence with the new project currently in development.

hero.headline: US and Iran sign agreement to end hostilities and reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding that took effect immediately after both countries finalized the agreement. President Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian signed the document on Wednesday, according to Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who served as the lead mediator in the negotiations.

The agreement marks a significant development in US-Iran relations, bringing an end to armed conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global energy supplies. Roughly one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied fossil gas passes through the narrow shipping channel during peacetime. The deal follows months of military engagement and tension between the two countries, with Pakistan playing a central role in facilitating the talks.

The 14-paragraph memo includes provisions ending the fighting and addresses Iran's nuclear program. The agreement also includes a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. President Trump has emphasized that the deal ensures Iran will never buy, develop, or produce a nuclear weapon.

Trump publicly defended the agreement, framing it as necessary to stabilize the region and restore normal shipping routes through the strait. The closure of the waterway had created serious economic consequences worldwide, with fuel price increases and supply disruptions affecting countries dependent on Gulf oil imports. Germany halved its 2026 growth forecast, while Greece announced additional economic aid for households and farmers struggling with increased energy costs.

The humanitarian impact of the conflict has been substantial. According to the International Maritime Organization, approximately 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships have been stranded in the Gulf since the strait's closure. The UN maritime agency has appealed for assistance for the stranded workers.

Despite the agreement, significant challenges remain unresolved. The text of the agreement regarding Iran's nuclear program falls short of Trump's public claims about the deal's guarantees. Critics argue that the most difficult aspects of US-Iran relations remain unaddressed, and the longer-term issues will require future negotiations to resolve. Some observers characterize the agreement as a return to conditions existing before the conflict began, rather than a comprehensive resolution of the underlying disputes.

Both sides have committed to the agreement's terms by signing the document, signaling their intention to move forward with implementation. The immediate effect means that provisions regarding the cessation of hostilities and the reopening of the strait are now in force. Pakistan's Prime Minister Sharif stated that the signing demonstrated genuine commitment from both Washington and Tehran to follow through on the outlined steps, though he acknowledged that talks scheduled in Islamabad did not proceed as originally planned.

cards.headline: Trump demands complicate Republican legislative priorities in Congress
cards.teaser: GOP lawmakers face tension as the president's recent requests arrive as they near completion of key policy objectives.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's interim deal with Iran has created fresh tensions within the Republican party. Several Senate Republicans, including Senator Bill Cassidy, have publicly criticized the agreement, calling it "the worst foreign policy blunder in decades." The accord, released Wednesday, includes significant political and financial concessions to Iran in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and averting economic crisis.

The deal's controversial terms have exposed divisions among GOP lawmakers, complicating efforts to maintain party unity. Republicans are now grappling with the administration's foreign policy direction while attempting to advance their broader legislative agenda in Congress.

cards.headline: Stock market gains increasingly influence Trump administration decisions
cards.teaser: The president has treated market performance as a measure of his presidency's success, affecting policy choices.
cards.body:
President Trump has increasingly relied on stock market performance as a guide for major decisions, treating market movements as immediate feedback on his administration. The president has cited market gains to justify consequential choices across multiple policy areas.

Trump's approach reflects his view of the stock market as a real-time measure of his presidency's effectiveness. This reliance on market signals has shaped his decision-making process on issues ranging from economic policy to diplomatic initiatives, with market reactions serving as a key factor in evaluating his choices.

cards.headline: House members seeking higher office face unusually high primary defeat rate
cards.teaser: Congressional representatives who left their seats to run for Senate or governor positions have lost primaries at elevated rates this cycle.
cards.body:
House members who ran for higher office instead of seeking reelection have experienced a poor track record in primary contests this year. They could end up with a higher rate of primary losses than in recent years.

The results suggest that congressional experience has not consistently translated into primary success for representatives attempting to move to the Senate or governor's office.

cards.headline: Senator Slotkin discusses intelligence confirmation and election security
cards.teaser: Michigan Democrat weighs in on the national intelligence director nomination process and surveillance authority renewal.
cards.body:
Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan addressed the ongoing confirmation process for a new national intelligence director and the pending renewal of intelligence surveillance tools. The Democratic senator also discussed concerns about election integrity in remarks made during an interview.

Slotkin's comments come as the Senate considers the nomination for the intelligence director position and debates the extension of spy program authorities. The Michigan senator has been vocal on national security matters since joining the Senate, bringing experience from her previous work in intelligence and defense policy.

cards.headline: Mangione's notebook writings may factor into defense strategy
cards.teaser: The manifesto found after Luigi Mangione's capture could play a role in his legal team's approach to the case.
cards.body:
Luigi Mangione's defense team plans to argue he was suffering from "extreme emotional disturbance" at the time UnitedHealth CEO Brian Thompson was killed. The notebook discovered after his capture, which contains writings described as a manifesto, may support this psychiatric defense strategy as legal proceedings continue.

The role these writings will play in establishing a mental health defense remains to be determined as the case moves forward.

cards.headline: First human trial tests cellular reprogramming for aging
cards.teaser: Clinical trial will determine if cells can be safely made younger in humans, a key test for longevity medicine.
cards.body:
The first human trial examining whether a drug can make human cells younger has begun, representing a significant test for longevity research. The early-stage clinical trial will assess whether cellular reprogramming can be performed safely in people, a requirement before any treatment could claim to slow or reverse biological aging.

The trial addresses one of the longevity field's central theories about extending human lifespan. Success in demonstrating safety would be necessary before researchers could advance claims about treatments that affect the aging process at the cellular level.
